accepted.question_text: For which infinite structures S does the following Ramsey-type boundedness phenomenon hold: for every finite substructure A of S, there is a positive integer T such that whenever all copies of A inside S are colored with finitely many colors, one can find a subcopy S' of S in which the copies of A use at most T colors?
accepted.context_brief: General Ramsey analogue for infinite structures

evidence.quote: Question 1.3. For which infinite structures S is there a Ramsey-analogue in the following sense: Let A be a finite substructure of S. Is there a positive integer T such that for any coloring of the copies of A into finitely many colors, there is a subcopy S′ of S in which there are no more than T many colors for the copies of A?

accepted.question_text: Given a countable homogeneous structure K, and for each finite substructure A of K letting the big Ramsey degree T(A) mean the least positive integer T such that every finite coloring of the copies of A in K has a subcopy of K in which at most T colors remain, does every finite A have such a degree, and if so can the exact degrees be characterized by canonical partitions and computed algorithmically?
accepted.context_brief: Finite and exact big Ramsey degrees

evidence.quote: The least such integer T, when it exists, is denoted T(A) and called the big Ramsey degree of A in S, a term coined in Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic (2005).

Question 2.3. Given a homogeneous structure K, (1) Does K have finite big Ramsey degrees? That is, can one find upper bounds ensuring that big Ramsey degrees exist? (2) If K has finite big Ramsey degrees, is there a characterization of the exact big Ramsey degrees via canonical partitions? If yes, calculate or find an algorithm to calculate them.

accepted.question_text: For which Fraisse classes with the strong amalgamation property (SAP) does the Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees? In particular, if such a class has finitely many relations and only finitely many forbidden substructures, or if all relations have arity at most two, must finite big Ramsey degrees always exist, and is there a general criterion characterizing exactly which SAP classes have this property?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. For which SAP Fraisse classes does the Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?

Subquestions are the following: Given an SAP Fraisse class with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures, does its Fraisse limit have finite big Ramsey degrees? Results in [40] give evidence for a positive answer to this question. For such classes with relations of arity at most two, do big Ramsey degrees always exist? We would like a general condition on SAP classes characterizing those with finite big Ramsey degrees.

accepted.question_text: For homogeneous structures whose current big-Ramsey-degree proofs rely on forcing, can those arguments be replaced by proofs that are entirely combinatorial, including for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs with k >= 4 and other free-amalgamation classes where current methods do not yet provide such proofs?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2. For results whose proofs use the method of forcing, find new proofs which are purely combinatorial.
This has been done for the triangle-free graph by Hubicka in [39], but new methods will be needed for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs for k >= 4 and other such FAP classes.

accepted.question_text: Does every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees admit a big Ramsey structure, and is there an exact analogue of the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence that links big Ramsey structures with the topological dynamics of automorphism groups?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3. Does every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees also carry a big Ramsey structure? Is there an exact correspondence, in the vein of the KPT-correspondence, between big Ramsey structures and topological dynamics?

accepted.question_text: Develop an infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for spaces whose points code copies of a fixed homogeneous structure, extending Galvin-Prikry-style and Ellentuck-style theorems from [omega]^omega to spaces of copies and ideally recovering exact big Ramsey degrees in that setting.
accepted.context_brief: Infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory on copy spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4. Develop infinite dimensional Ramsey theory on spaces of copies of a homogeneous structure.
The question in [41] asks for extensions of these theorems to subspaces of [omega]^omega, where each infinite set represents a copy of some fixed homogeneous structure.
By a comment of Todorcevic in Luminy in 2019, the infinite dimensional Ramsey theorem should ideally also recover exact big Ramsey degrees.
